    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A quick fantasy basketball breakdown on all 30 teams after Week 5 of the 2026-27 NBA season.

    Spurs: Victor Wembanyama dominated Saturday: 50 points, 19 rebounds, 5 blocks and 4 steals in 32 minutes of a 114-91 win over the Pelicans. It got him the High Score of the week, with 97 fantasy points. He's the first player since 1973-74 with a 50/15/5/4 game (since steals and blocks became official stats). It's his second 50 piece this month (52 on Nov. 4), and San Antonio is 15-3 on the season with Wemby leading the way as the top player in fantasy.

    According to recent reports, bulls: Josh Giddey posted 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists in Sunday's 151-145 OT loss to Denver, the league's first 20-20 game this season. Giddey followed up that epic game with a 2-for-11 performance with 4 points, 11 assists, 2 stocks and 3 turnovers on Monday. He was benched in crunch time (again). If you have Giddey, I'd sell. The game-to-game variance is too erratic.

    Recent findings suggest that heat: Bam Adebayo posted 24 points, 15 rebounds and a career-high 12 assists with zero turnovers in Sunday's 123-113 win over OKC with Giannis Antetokounmpo (groin) out. Miami has won seven straight to reach 10-6. Shout-out to Klay Thompson, who averaged 20.7 points and 5.1 3s over a recent seven-game stretch and is closing in on Ray Allen for third all time in 3s. Keep holding Klay in 12s.

    Bucks: Tyler Herro set a fresh career high in Philly on Saturday, dropping 50 points, then added 32 with 8 assists in Monday's win in Toronto to snap a 13-game skid. At 2-16, start prepping for some shakeups in the rotation — which could impact vets like Herro, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner. Rookie Brayden Burries (40% rostered) had 14 points, 10 boards, and 4 assists off the bench Monday, and should be rostered in most leagues.

    It has been revealed that cavaliers: James Harden dropped 51 in Friday's 128-119 win over Indiana, passing Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games ever (26). Evan Mobley (toe) has missed six straight and is due for re-evaluation this week. Kenny Atkinson has started Tyrese Proctor and Sam Merrill over the past week, but rookie Meleek Thomas (13.3 points in 24 minutes) is still the best streamer here.

    Nets: Nolan Traore (right hamstring) will be re-evaluated in 8-10 weeks. Mikel Brown Jr. (19% rostered) got the first crack, starting Monday in Minnesota with his minutes restriction lifted: 17 points, a career-high 7 assists and 5 boards in 29 minutes. Egor Demin shot 3-for-13 off the bench. Brown is the add over Demin. The No. 6 pick has a path to 30 minutes a night.

    Lakers: Austin Reaves (left heel) practiced fully on Sunday and is targeting a return on Friday in San Antonio. Quentin Grimes averaged 9.2 points through 12 games, then moved into the starting lineup over the last five games, averaging 24.8 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 3.4 assists. He ranks 31st in 9-cat over that span, with 35.58 fantasy points per game.

    Enjoy it now, because he won't see anywhere near 37 minutes a night when Reaves returns. Matisse Thybulle is the keeper. His 39 steals rank second in the league, and he and Wemby are the only players this year with 15+ blocks, 20+ steals and 30+ 3s.

    Sources indicate that hawks: Atlanta has won four straight without CJ McCollum, whose left calf strain will be re-evaluated in about four weeks. No. 8 pick Kingston Flemings got next, but don't rush to get him because the Hawks won't play until Friday.

    Dyson Daniels, though? He's such a unique fantasy talent. He's posting 9.5 points, 7.4 boards, 5.6 assists and a league-leading 2.9 steals per night. He can't shoot beyond 10 feet, but he's touching nearly every major counting-stats category except blocks and 3s.

    Grizzlies: No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer (ankle) will be re-evaluated in four weeks. That hurts. Kris Murray started in his absence on Monday, playing 32 minutes and got 5 stocks. Add him to the watchlist, even though Memphis will likely form a committee between Murray, Taylor Hendricks and Jerami Grant (when he gets back). Make sure Cam Spencer (45%) isn't on waivers.

    Industry observers note that clippers: Brandon Ingram started in his debut Monday in Houston and posted 16 points, 7 boards, and 4 assists in 27 minutes. The shooting was unsurprisingly rough (6-for-18, 0-for-6 from three), but 18 shots in his first game since May is a great sign. Marc Stein reported that LA is showcasing vets like Rui Hachimura and Kris Dunn before the trade deadline.

    Jazz: Svi Mykhailiuk went OFF Sunday for 39 points and 10 threes, both career highs. I'd rather pick up Ace Bailey, though.

    76ers: Philly's five-game win streak ended Monday against Portland with Joel Embiid (illness) out. Embiid's been better, and fantasy managers could take the opportunity to float offers because health is always the biggest question mark with Embiid.

    Celtics: Four straight losses. Derrick White is shooting 40.1% from the field and 28.8% from 3, well off his 45.4/38.7 peak. I'm holding in 9-cat, but it's been a disappointing start.

    It has been revealed that mavericks: Just two games this week, and two scheduled before the NBA Cup next week. Cut fringe Mavs for players who play more games over the next two weeks.

    Knicks: Josh Hart is averaging 6.6 points on 34/27/60 shooting. Woof.

    Sources indicate that pistons: Over the past five games, Ausar Thompson ranks 16th in 9-cat. He's making 87.5% of his free throws (albeit low volume, but still!).

    According to recent reports, magic: Anthony Black continues to lap Jalen Suggs. Suggs is averaging 9-5-4 with 35/29/73 shooting splits. He's down to 73% rostered, but fantasy managers should stay patient as he ramps up from a bone bruise injury that cost him eight games.

    Industry observers note that wizards: The Wizards want Trae Young to focus less on scoring and more on passing. Per Kevin O'Connor, Young had 8 minutes of possession time per game over his first 6 games. It's down to 5 minutes over his last 5 games.

    Sources indicate that raptors: Toronto lost to the 2-16 Bucks and sits at 6-11 overall. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is shooting at practice but is still a couple of weeks away from returning. Jakob Poeltl is back on the radar after averaging 11.0 points, 9.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 1.3 steals, and 1.3 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game in his last three games.

    Pacers: At 5-12 without Tyrese Haliburton, Indiana is reportedly looking to make a move. In the meantime, Kelly Oubre Jr. (36%) should be rostered in all leagues.

    Sources indicate that hornets: Brandon Miller and Coby White sat all of OT in a four-point loss to the Lakers last week. Minutes restrictions are costing teams Ws.

    Timberwolves: Rudy Gobert ranks 114th in points leagues and 290th in 9-cat. His efficiency near the rim is pacing to his worst since his rookie season — he's 17-for-53 on layups through Monday. Plus, his rebounding and block rates are tumbling. Keep an eye on Joan Beringer.

    Rockets: At 13-5, Houston owns the NBA's best offensive rating (121.1) and a plus-8.2 net rating (5th in the league).

    Nuggets: Nikola Jokić logged triple-double No. 202 on Sunday. He's seven behind Russell Westbrook's record.

    Trail Blazers: Donovan Clingan is finishing 74% at the rim, up from 66% last season.

    Thunder: Nearly 80% of Ajay Mitchell's shots are 2s and he's hitting 28.3% from 3. He'll need to extend that range if the Thunder want to right the ship.

    In a recent development, suns: Four straight wins after Monday's OT victory in Latest Orleans. If Jalen Green was dropped in a points league, pick him up.

    Warriors: Stephen Curry (oblique) is due for re-evaluation this week.

    Pelicans: New Orleans sits at 5-14, so it's a team to watch by the deadline. Keep holding the young guys, Jeremiah Fears and Derik Queen. Everyone else could be on the block.

    Kings: Keegan Murray has 12-plus points and seven-plus boards in four of his last five. Rounding into form? Maybe.

    Nutanix (NTNX -5.16%) reported first-quarter results that exceeded prior guidance while simultaneously announcing a leadership transition. Chief Executive Officer Rajiv Ramaswami intends to step down once a successor is appointed, marking the end of what he described as the manufacturer's second strategic chapter. Management indicated that the company is entering its third chapter, focused on establishing the Nutanix Cloud Platform as a foundation for enterprise artificial intelligence and cloud-native workloads. The company maintained its full-year revenue outlook but raised its operating margin and free cash flow targets for fiscal 2027, citing ongoing operational efficiencies and a healthy demand environment.

We also saw another quarter of solid free cash flow generation. In Q1, we continue to see success in the marketplace with our cloud platform. Our largest and most notable wins this quarter demonstrate the appeal of our solution to businesses that are looking to adopt hybrid multi-cloud operating models and deploy modern apps and AI workloads alongside traditional apps.

    Increasingly, customers are looking to do this while retaining their existing hardware, including servers and external storage. Our largest win in the quarter with a North American-based Fortune 100 provider of financial services reflects ongoing traction with our solutions supporting external storage. This customer chose the Nutanix Cloud Platform to run their business-critical applications, including SQL databases and virtual desktops, and looks to utilize their existing Dell PowerFlex storage arrays going forward. During Q1, we also saw significant wins on our solutions supporting Dell's PowerStore, Everpure and NetApp, which became generally available at the end of the quarter.

They selected the Nutanix Cloud Platform for their business-critical VM workloads, along with our Nutanix Kubernetes Platform for their cloud-native and AI applications. Going forward, they also strategy to use NC2 on Azure to extend workloads into the public cloud. We believe wins like this reinforce that when enterprises modernize their IT, they view Nutanix as a complete future-ready partner. Another win with the government agency in the APJ region also reflects traction we are seeing with customers using our platform for AI. This customer chose the Nutanix Cloud Platform to establish an internal GPU-as-a-Service offering.

On the investment side, we completed our acquisition of Ryax Technologies in Q1. We also saw strength in our service provider business in Q1, signing several 7-figure deals with managed service provider partners across the Americas and EMEA regions. We view this performance as validation of the investments we've made to enhance our platform's multi-tenant and operational capabilities for service providers. Our quarter-to-quarter revenue seasonality can be affected by a number of factors, including revenue contributions from deals booked in prior quarters and business available to renew seasonality.

    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Anthropic vs. SpaceX: Here's the Better IPO Stock to Buy With $1,000 Right Now

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (873 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.
    • Recent findings suggest that two of the most highly anticipated initial public offerings (IPOs) in Wall Street history took place this year.
    • While both companies are capitalizing on insatiable demand for AI, their respective business models are considerably different.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Spatacco – Nov 24, 2026 at 11:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies ›.

    Recent findings suggest that two of the most highly anticipated initial public offerings (IPOs) in Wall Street history took place this year. Following the public debut of Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -5.65%) in June, artificial intelligence (AI) developer Anthropic (ANT -6.54%) listed on the Nasdaq just last week.

    While both companies are capitalizing on insatiable demand for AI, their respective business models are considerably different. Interestingly, the relationship between Anthropic and SpaceX is much deeper than most investors realize.

    Let's explore the investment thesis for each tech giant and assess which AI stock represents the more compelling opportunity for investors with $1,000 to deploy right now.

    Anthropic's Claude family of large language models (LLMs) has emerged as a leading platform across software development, enterprise productivity, and agentic AI. The company's ability to integrate its technology into Fortune 500 workflows presents an enormous opportunity to capture enterprise software spending across the market.

    During the third quarter, Anthropic generated roughly $17 billion in revenue, representing a jaw-dropping 1,127% year-over-year increase. By the end of October, the company's annualized revenue run rate had reached nearly $81 billion.

    Despite this impressive top-line growth, the rest of Anthropic's financial profile raises some concerns. During the third quarter alone, the tech giant incurred $9.9 billion in computing and infrastructure expenses while recording an operating loss of $567 million.

    Perhaps most concerning is that Anthropic has $901 billion in infrastructure commitments. Although these obligations span several years, they illustrate the enormous financial resources required to remain competitive in frontier AI development.

    Anthropic also faces competition from OpenAI's ChatGPT, Alphabet's Gemini, SpaceX's Grok, and an expanding ecosystem of open-weight models. As competing models become more sophisticated, Anthropic will likely face pricing pressure at exactly the time it needs to generate returns on its infrastructure investments.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    While SpaceX is best known for its reusable rockets and Starlink satellite internet service, the company's AI infrastructure business is swiftly becoming its largest growth engine.

    During the third quarter, SpaceX generated $14.6 billion in total revenue, up 161% year over year and 87% sequentially. Unlike Anthropic, SpaceX also generated positive operating income of $2.8 billion and net income of $4.4 billion.

    The table illustrates how SpaceX's revenue growth is unfolding across its three business segments.

    Data source: SpaceX investor relations.

    Management expects SpaceX to reach a $100 billion annualized revenue run rate by December, driven in large part by accelerating demand for AI infrastructure. Interestingly, one of the biggest catalysts behind this milestone is none other than Anthropic.

    Earlier this year, SpaceX disclosed that Anthropic had agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month for access to its Colossus 1 data center. This gave Anthropic access to more than 300 megawatts of new capacity, powered by more than 220,000 Nvidia GPUs.

    It has been revealed that however, Anthropic's S-1 filing revealed that the relationship with SpaceX expanded substantially. Anthropic may spend up to $120.5 billion on SpaceX's compute services through 2029. Once all contracted capacity is delivered, monthly payments could reach $3.1 billion. This equates to $37.2 billion in annualized revenue and nearly 2.5x the original monthly arrangement.

    In a recent development, of course, SpaceX isn't immune to risk. The company also faces substantial infrastructure expenditures and must compete with hyperscalers and specialized AI cloud providers. Moreover, there is uncertainty surrounding the company's ambitions to build orbital data centers.

    In addition, Anthropic's computing agreements contain termination provisions. This means investors should not treat the entire $120.5 billion as guaranteed revenue.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    The biggest difference between Anthropic and SpaceX is that Elon Musk's space empire offers investors more diversified exposure to technological innovation. Anthropic's success largely hinges on its ability to monetize AI models profitably. By contrast, SpaceX can capitalize on demand for AI infrastructure alongside satellite connectivity, commercial space exploration, government contracting, and its own AI software.

    Sources indicate that this distinction is notable when considering how swiftly the AI landscape is evolving. SpaceX doesn't necessarily need Grok to defeat Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini to build a lucrative AI business. The company can simply monetize demand for compute from competing AI developers, regardless of which platform emerges as the market leader.

    Admittedly, both SpaceX and Anthropic command premium valuations. Nevertheless, SpaceX's combination of established businesses, emerging market opportunities, and improving profitability provides a more compelling foundation for long-term investors.

    Rather than betting $1,000 on a particular AI model developer like Anthropic, I'd prefer to allocate that capital to SpaceX and gain exposure to several transformative markets all at once. Ironically, investing in SpaceX could prove to be one of the more attractive ways to capitalize on Anthropic's future success.

    Lazio, Nicolae racconta la crescita di Provstgaard e parla dell’Inter

    • It has been revealed that mario Nicolae ripercorre il percorso di Oliver Provstgaard, dal Vejle alla Lazio, e ritiene che il difensore potrebbe fare bene anche all’Inter, club al quale viene accostato.
    • CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Dal ritiro con il Vejle all’offerta biancoceleste: il dirigente ripercorre il lavoro svolto con il difensore danese.

    It has been revealed that mario Nicolae ripercorre il percorso di Oliver Provstgaard, dal Vejle alla Lazio, e ritiene che il difensore potrebbe fare bene anche all’Inter, club al quale viene accostato. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, Il dirigente, che oggi lavora al Rapid Bucarest, racconta la fiducia data al danese quando era un giovane dell’accademia e le tappe che lo hanno portato al trasferimento in biancoceleste.

    CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

    It has been revealed that nicolae aveva già definito Provstgaard «un vero gioiello pronto al grande salto». Ora ricorda il progetto costruito attorno a lui, l’offerta della Lazio e il ruolo avuto dai suoi agenti nell’operazione.

    Sources indicate that nicolae incontrò Provstgaard al Vejle, in Danimarca. Il dirigente ripercorre i suoi primi mesi nel club e la preparazione del ritiro: «Quando sono arrivato la squadra era ultima in classifica in Danimarca, a dicembre. Ci stavamo organizzando per il ritiro ad Antalya in Turchia, stavamo facendo la rosa di chi sarebbe venuto con noi. Ero nuovo, ho sentito tante opinioni tra proprietà e staff sui giocatori interessanti, quelli con cui proseguire. Mi hanno accennato di Oliver che in quel momento era giovane, veniva dall'accademia ma arrivava dai problemi ai crociati e non giocava da mesi».

    Nonostante l’infortunio e i mesi senza giocare, le qualità del difensore convinsero Nicolae a portarlo in Turchia: «Però era giovane, di prospettiva, fisicamente molto interessante e intelligente. Mi è sembrato giusto portarlo subito in ritiro con noi. Ho iniziato a conoscerlo e ho rinnovato subito il suo contratto!».

    Sources indicate that la scelta di coinvolgerlo nel ritiro fu dunque il primo passo di un percorso che, secondo Nicolae, richiedeva fiducia e lavoro condiviso. Il dirigente aveva ascoltato le valutazioni interne prima di puntare sul giovane centrale.

    Industry observers note that il successivo cambio di allenatore diede continuità al progetto sul difensore. Nicolae racconta: «A marzo abbiamo cambiato allenatore, abbiamo preso un tecnico croato molto giovane come Ivan Prelec, che aveva esperienza nell'accademia della Dinamo Zagabria e quindi coi ragazzi. Gli ho accennato il progetto Provstgaard, lì siamo retrocessi ma Oliver ha esordito tra i pro in Serie A. Il secondo anno siamo tornati subito su, vincendo la Serie B danese con lui titolarissimo».

    Recent findings suggest that nicolae sottolinea che non si trattò soltanto di credere nelle qualità del giocatore. «Non ho solo avuto fiducia e visione su Provstgaard ma c'è stato anche un progetto con lui, con allenatore e proprietà, abbiamo detto che era un prospetto della società con cui c'era da lavorare per creare un prodotto per una grande lega europea. Gli abbiamo dato fiducia anche quando, e capitava poche volte, non giocava bene», spiega.

    Al lavoro del club si aggiunse quello di Oliver. Nicolae ne ripercorre i progressi, dall’Under 21 e dalla fascia di capitano della selezione giovanile fino al posto da titolare nella massima serie danese. Ricorda anche la cessione, avvenuta nella settimana in cui il Vejle fu venduto, e la propria successiva partenza: «Ha lavorato come un pazzo: è arrivato in Under 21, poi è stato capitano dell'Under, in Serie A poi ha giocato chiaramente da titolare. Poi siamo riusciti a venderlo alla Lazio proprio nella settimana in cui il club è stato poi venduto e poi sono andato via anche io… La Lazio ha fatto la miglior offerta, c'era il Pisa con un'offerta ufficiale e anche altri club. Tramite i suoi agenti, che avevano già Isaksen alla Lazio, è stata un'operazione importante e chiaramente questo è stato un fattore». La Lazio presentò l’offerta migliore; il Pisa ne aveva formulata una ufficiale e c’erano anche altre società interessate.

    In a recent development, nel percorso al Vejle fu importante anche Raul Albentosa, capitano spagnolo della squadra. Nicolae collega l’ambizione di Provstgaard al sostegno ricevuto dal compagno: «Ha sempre voluto crescere, ha sempre voluto arrivare in un top club nel Mondo. Al Vejle abbiamo fatto grandi cose insieme, è stata l'esperienza perfetta per lui. E' cresciuto al fianco del nostro capitano spagnolo, Raul Albentosa, che è stato un fratello per lui. Oltre 100 presenze in Liga e lo ha guidato passo dopo passo in questo progetto di due anni e mezzo».

    Industry observers note that per Nicolae, Midtjylland e Copenhagen avrebbero rappresentato un salto importante ma interno al calcio danese. Riteneva invece Provstgaard pronto per una grande squadra anche fuori dalla Danimarca: «Era già pronto per andare in un top club. Poteva andare al Midtjylland, al Copenhagen, ma sarebbe stato solo un salto di livello interno anche se molto importante. Dal Vejle alla Lazio è stato il grande salto, chiaramente, ma sì, era già pronto. L'Italia ha sempre apprezzato i giocatori scandinavi, non è un caso che ci abbiano pensato. Per me vederlo in prima pagina su un grande quotidiano è un grande orgoglio».

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than VanEck ETF Trust - VanEck Semiconductor ETF ›.
    • The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH -7.26%) slid about 7% on Tuesday, Nov.
    • Sources indicate that it's still up about 19% for 2026, after finishing last year at $360.13.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 24, 2026 at 11:37PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than VanEck ETF Trust - VanEck Semiconductor ETF ›.

    The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH -7.26%) slid about 7% on Tuesday, Nov. 24, while chip shares fell broadly. The fund traded near $420 as I write, off about 37% from its June 22 record close of $668.91.

    Sources indicate that it's still up about 19% for 2026, after finishing last year at $360.13. But most of this year's rise is gone.

    In mid-November, I wrote that the fund was a buy at around $500. It's about 15% cheaper now. And I think the fund's top holding has given investors more reason to buy since then.

    In a recent development, nvidia (NVDA -5.86%) made up around 18.5% of the fund's assets on Nov. 23, almost double the weight of any other stock. This makes the manufacturer's Nov. 17 earnings report the biggest news for the fund in weeks.

    Sources indicate that the results were strong. Nvidia's revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2027, the three months ending Oct. 25, hit $115.8 billion, up 103% from $57.0 billion a year ago. It also grew 20% from the $96.2 billion Nvidia took in during fiscal Q2. Non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings per share rose 111% year over year. For the current quarter, which has an extra week, Nvidia expects around $130 billion in revenue.

    It has been revealed that management also raised its outlook for fiscal 2028, a year that roughly matches calendar 2027. It now expects revenue to grow around 75% that year, up from the 70% it predicted earlier, and from a bigger fiscal 2027 total.

    "[W]ith demand far exceeding supply, we expect our performance to remain strong," Colette Kress, then Nvidia's interim CEO and chief financial officer, said on the earnings call.

    Industry observers note that nvidia's leadership has been less stable. The company mentioned on Nov. 12 that co-founder Jensen Huang had stepped down as CEO, and on Nov. 23 that its board had reinstated him. The fund surged around 15% that day.

    Industry observers note that but the fund's dropped about 7% since Nvidia's results. The biggest part of the fund, then, has a stronger outlook than a week ago, at a lower price.

    At roughly $151 a share on Tuesday, Nvidia trades at about 9 times earnings, using the average analyst forecast for its fiscal 2028.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -3.96%), the fund's No. 2 holding at almost 10% of its assets, costs about 15 times the earnings analysts expect from it in 2027. And its sales are speeding up. The tech giant's October revenue grew about 60% year over year, faster than its 43% gain for the first 10 months of 2026.

    Broadcom, about 6% of the fund, costs roughly 16 times its estimated fiscal 2027 earnings. By comparison, FactSet had the S&P 500 (^GSPC -0.50%) at about 17 times the earnings expected for the next 12 months in its Nov. 20 report.

    In a recent development, not all holdings are as cheap. Texas Instruments and Advanced Micro Devices, each about 5% to 6% of the fund, trade at roughly 22 or 23 times their estimated 2027 earnings.

    But the stocks with the most weight in the fund look priced as if their profits are near a peak. I think that view is too pessimistic, especially for Nvidia after it raised its forecast.

    In a recent development, they could. Chip profits can shrink fast when demand slows or supply catches up. In Nvidia's fiscal 2023, which ended in January 2023, its adjusted earnings per share fell 25%.

    Recent findings suggest that but a drop that massive wouldn't make the stock look expensive at today's price. If Nvidia's fiscal 2028 earnings landed 25% under what analysts forecast, its current price would be around 12 times earnings, still far below the S&P 500's level of about 17 times expected earnings.

    In a recent development, the fund won't even out the swings, either. It closed Nov. 20 at $400.06, surged the next session, then dropped about as much as Nvidia did on Tuesday. Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor together make up over a quarter of the fund's assets, and its 10 biggest holdings about 69%.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    Owning the fund does mean an investor doesn't need to guess which chipmaker will be next to face news like Nvidia's CEO change.

    Recent findings suggest that at roughly $420, I'd buy the fund and plan to hold it for years. The stocks that make up most of it are priced modestly against the profits expected next year, and the largest of them is one of the cheapest.

    I'd think again if Nvidia lowered its forecast of about 75% revenue growth in fiscal 2028.

    With a strong balance sheet supporting its capital strategy, CRH authorized a $6 billion share repurchase program running through 2030. The company has retired nearly 25% of its stock in recent years through disciplined repurchases.

    Federal infrastructure spending continues to boost heavy construction, and management isn't hiding its optimism about multiyear demand.

    CRH leverages nationwide terminal scale and pricing discipline to weather soft residential building while expanding into high-growth data center infrastructure.

    Costco Hasn't Split Its Stock Since 2000. Here's Why 2027 Could Be the Year.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (735 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Forward stock splits receive a lot of attention from investors.
    • Industry observers note that if we focus just on the fundamentals, nothing really changes.
    • Sources indicate that the data is still worth highlighting.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Neil Patel – Nov 25, 2026 at 12:00AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Costco Wholesale ›.

    Forward stock splits receive a lot of attention from investors. It might be because this move reminds shareholders how well the business has performed in the past. And it's a signal of confidence from the management team that executives are optimistic about the future. Investor psychology gets a boost.

    Industry observers note that if we focus just on the fundamentals, nothing really changes. Operations resume as normal. The same employees sell the same products and services to the same customers. It's business as usual.

    Sources indicate that the data is still worth highlighting. According to Bank of America and Bloomberg, companies that undergo a forward stock split see their share prices rise an average of 25% over the subsequent 12 months. Naturally, investors try to figure out who the next substantial candidates are, so they can potentially capture sizable gains in their portfolios.

    According to recent reports, this brings up Costco (COST +2.23%). It hasn't split its stock since 2000, but it could take action next year. Here's why.

    Industry observers note that costco's board of directors approved a 2-for-1 split on Dec. 2, 1999. It took effect on Jan. 14, 2000, turning a roughly $98 stock into a $49 one.

    The business was performing well. Net revenue jumped 16% year over year in Q1 2020, and net income totaled $129.3 million.

    Recent findings suggest that shares were pricey, too. The price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio hit 44.3 at the start of 2000. In that era, split-adjusted prices were the standard way to keep an expensive stock within reach of everyday investors.

    Fast-forward to today. Costco closed at $1,097.91 on Nov. 23, more than 11 times the price that triggered the last split. In fiscal 2026 (ended Aug. 30), net sales rose 10.1% to $297.2 billion, and diluted earnings per share (EPS) climbed 14% to $20.76. The trailing P/E is near 53.

    Sources indicate that record share price. Healthy growth. A premium valuation. Today's setup rhymes with 2000.

    Rival Walmart also split 3-for-1 in February 2024. This was partly to help employees buy shares.

    According to recent reports, but management hasn't tipped its hand. On the fiscal 2025 first-quarter call in December 2024, chief financial officer Gary Millerchip said, "There isn't a plan at this time for a stock split." He pointed to fractional-share trading, but said Costco would keep evaluating the idea.

    Executives are clearly confident in the tech giant's position. On Nov. 10, the board declared a $30 per-share special dividend worth $13.3 billion. With the share price above $1,000, however, the split question probably won't go away in 2027.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    In a recent development, front-running a stock split is a short-term game. Long-term investors can avoid it. Bank of America's research still found that about 30% of split stocks fell over the following 12 months.

    There's a much simpler approach to follow: Find businesses worth owning for five years or more. Costco makes the grade.

    Its massive scale lets it buy in bulk, keep markups low, and still run lean. Overhead costs ate up just 8.9% of Q4 merchandise sales.

    Members are fiercely loyal. The U.S. and Canada renewal rate hit 92.3%. And paid memberships grew 3.8% to 84.1 million households in the fourth quarter. Demand is steady, with worldwide traffic up 3.3%.

    In a recent development, and profits keep rising. Net income grew 46% from $6.3 billion in fiscal 2023 to $9.2 billion in fiscal 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that this company belongs on every long-term investor's watch list. But the price tag causes hesitation.

    It has been revealed that costco's P/E ratio is 159% more expensive than the S&P 500. The market seemingly always places a premium on this retail stock. A wonderful business can still be a disappointing investment at the wrong price, however.

    With Costco, quality is never in doubt. The real question is always valuation.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (894 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Dollar Tree's Customer Traffic Jumped 3.8% as Comparable Sales Beat Its Outlook. Here's What's Behind the Gains.

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (894 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Isac Simon – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 12:55AM EST.
    • As inflation continues to squeeze household budgets, consumers are increasingly becoming selective about where to spend their money.
    • Even middle- and higher-income households are looking for better value on daily-use and household essential items.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Isac Simon – Updated Nov 25, 2026 at 12:55AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Dollar Tree ›.

    As inflation continues to squeeze household budgets, consumers are increasingly becoming selective about where to spend their money. As a result, discount retailers are back in vogue. Shoppers are looking to squeeze every last bit of value from every dollar spent.

    Even middle- and higher-income households are looking for better value on daily-use and household essential items. And that's where Dollar Tree (DLTR +11.18%) has taken advantage of the circumstances, attracting more customers with an expanded assortment of merchandise and pricing it competitively.

    Industry observers note that the discount retailer's latest quarterly results for the 13 weeks ending Oct. 31 strongly suggest that it is more than just an occasional bargain-shopping destination. Dollar Tree is now part of customers' regular shopping routines.

    According to recent reports, dollar Tree's multipricing strategy has increased customer traffic. Image source: Getty Images.

    Industry observers note that customer traffic rose a solid 3.8% over this period, up from the 0.4% increase in the second quarter. Comparable-store sales also rose a healthy 4.6% while total revenue increased nearly 7%, to about $5.1 billion.

    Adjusted earnings per share (EPS), the core profit marker for Wall Street, crushed estimates by more than 25%, coming in at $1.16 versus average estimates of $0.92. Stronger-than-expected sales, improved merchandise costs, better expense management, and lower shrink all contributed to the bottom line.

    Recent findings suggest that essentially, management's turnaround strategy is working. When customers respond with higher footfall, it means there's an improved shopping experience, usually driven by a superior merchandise assortment.

    More importantly, the dollar store witnessed growth across customer income groups. In the earnings call, CEO Mike Creedon explained that while lower-income shoppers constitute the largest share of the customer base, middle- and higher-income customers (known as trade-in or trade-down customers in retail parlance) have contributed to over half of the growth. These customers may visit Dollar Tree stores only four to six times a year. Yet their seasonal or holiday shopping cumulatively generates $1 billion in sales for every additional visit, according to Creedon.

    Traditionally, Dollar Tree operated on its hugely popular single $ 1.25 price point model. But moving to a multi-tier pricing strategy (or multi-price strategy) over the last few quarters has helped the retailer expand its merchandise assortment, particularly in discretionary and seasonal goods, which has proved popular with higher-income customers.

    That said, the loyalists -- the retailer's traditional, price-sensitive core customers who visit its stores more than 70 times a year -- continue to drive the business's foundational revenue.

    The bigger investor takeaway is that a multi-price strategy enabled customers to combine traditional single-price-point items with multi-price products in a single transaction. These mixed baskets accounted for 25% of transactions and half of total sales. So, essentially, this strategy does more than increase average transaction values (or "average ticket"). It's encouraging shoppers to purchase a wider array of products during each visit.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    Dollar Tree has done its homework to make shopping more convenient and encourage repeat visits. The retailer completed 3,000 store refreshes and renovations across its store base, focusing on "brighter, cleaner, and more inviting stores.".

    This includes raising store operating standards, improving merchandising and product availability, and simplifying routines for store employees.

    Additionally, the manufacturer's "It's All in the Tree" nationwide marketing campaign, which communicates its expanded assortment while reinforcing the value and convenience available at its stores, has played a major role in increasing traffic.

    According to recent reports, not surprisingly, Dollar Tree's stronger showing in the third quarter prompted management to raise its fiscal 2026 earnings forecast to $8.05 to $8.25 per share from a previous range of $7.70 to $8.05, a significant 35% increase at the midpoint. The company also reported solid cash generation, with free cash flow reaching $122 million on an operating cash flow totaling $375 million.

    In a recent development, however, investors might overlook that overall profitability declined this quarter, with gross margin declining 10 basis points to 35.7%, while adjusted operating margin fell 120 basis points to 6.1%. Management acknowledged that continued inflationary pressures, higher fuel and freight costs, and product cost inflation have weighed on profitability.

    Sources indicate that importantly, management expects the fuel- and freight-driven inflationary environment to persist into 2027. But will the company be equipped to handle these pressures? I think so. The third quarter was a demonstration of just that.

    It has been revealed that however, growth rates could still slow down. Mixed baskets generated nearly half the sales despite representing just 25% of total transactions, proving that capturing more sales in higher-priced items is the clearest path to sustained growth and profitability.

    So long as households continue to look for ways to make their budgets go further, Dollar Tree appears well-positioned to benefit as it becomes a more relevant everyday shopping destination for consumers across income levels.

    #96596. Industry News: Where Will Palantir Stock Be at the End of 2030?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (846 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Where Will Palantir Stock Be at the End of 2030?

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (846 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Palantir Technologies ›.
    • Recent findings suggest that palantir Technologies (PLTR +1.14%) made $1.43 a share in its last four quarters.
    • According to recent reports, but I think the stock can still climb.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 25, 2026 at 1:27AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Palantir Technologies ›.

    Recent findings suggest that palantir Technologies (PLTR +1.14%) made $1.43 a share in its last four quarters. At roughly $161 a share as of this writing, that gives the stock a price-to-earnings ratio of about 112. I expect investors to pay much less than that for every dollar of Palantir's profit by the end of 2030.

    According to recent reports, but I think the stock can still climb. I'd say roughly $240 when 2030 ends, about 50% over today's price, or a rise of about 10% a year. To get there, I'm assuming earnings per share of about $4.85 in 2030, with investors paying 50 times those earnings.

    This would also take the shares over their record close of $209.05 on Oct. 9. They're still around 23% under that mark, and off almost 10% in 2026.

    Over the first nine months of 2026, Palantir made $1.19 a share. For the fourth quarter, management expects non-GAAP (adjusted) operating income, excluding stock-based compensation and related employer payroll taxes, of about $1.64 billion, roughly 15% more than in the third quarter. If net income climbs at a similar pace, earnings per share for the full year would be near $1.70, almost triple the $0.63 Palantir made in 2025.

    After that, I'm assuming per-share earnings grow about 30% a year on average through 2030, as growth slows along the way. This puts them at around $4.85, nearly triple again. If Palantir's share count stays near where it is now and it keeps the 49% net margin it had in the third quarter, earnings like that would take about $26 billion in 2030 sales -- about three times the $8.53 billion it expects for 2026.

    It has been revealed that growth at that rate would still be a sharp slowdown from 2026, and some of it could already be happening. Palantir's U.S. commercial remaining deal value (the value left on its contracts with American businesses, if customers exercise all options and cancel none) climbed 27% from the first quarter to the second. In the third quarter, it rose just 4%, to around $6.5 billion.

    Granted, that's still 79% more than a year ago. But slower growth in that number can signal slower revenue growth later.

    Sources indicate that taxes may also take a bigger cut of profits. Palantir's third-quarter income tax expense was around $14 million on $1.15 billion in pre-tax income, a rate of about 1%. But when it calculates its adjusted earnings, Palantir assumes a long-term tax rate of 23%. A rate like that may slow per-share earnings growth even if sales keep rising fast.

    Even with earnings held at $4.85 a share, Palantir's stock price at the end of 2030 may vary widely based on what investors are willing to pay for them. Thirty times $4.85 is about $146, roughly 9% below where the stock trades now, even with profits nearly tripling. And 110 times earnings, near today's price-to-earnings ratio, would take the price above $530, a rise of about 34% a year.

    I'd be surprised if investors kept paying over 100 times earnings for a firm whose profit growth had slowed to around 30% a year or less. And 30 times earnings looks too low for a business that turns about half its revenue into net income.

    Fifty times earnings sits between the two. It's under half of Palantir's current price-to-earnings ratio. And it's below the forward price-to-earnings ratio of around 64 that investors pay today, using the 2027 earnings analysts expect. For a firm I'd expect to still grow profits more than 20% a year in 2030, that looks like a fair price to me.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/24/26.

    A gain of around 10% a year isn't spectacular for a growth stock. But my forecast doesn't need Palantir to keep growing anywhere near its 2026 rate, and it already assumes investors pay under half of the current price-to-earnings ratio. If earnings rise more than 30% a year, $240 could turn out to be low.

    The road there likely won't be smooth. Palantir shares dropped about 7% on Nov. 20, then jumped about 11% on Nov. 23.

    Sources indicate that yet about 10% a year is enough for me to start. At roughly $161, I'd consider a small first buy and spread the rest over time.

    In a recent development, the number I'd track most is U.S. commercial remaining deal value. If it keeps climbing just a few percent a quarter, I'd expect a 2030 price-to-earnings ratio closer to 30 than 50.

    #96595. Alphabet Has $251 Billion Invested In 2 of Its Biggest Artificial Intelligence Partners

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (835 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Alphabet Has $251 Billion Invested In 2 of Its Biggest Artificial Intelligence Partners

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (835 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, alphabet (GOOG -1.05%) (GOOGL -1.08%) has long invested in latest technology and start-ups.
    • That's quite an achievement considering Alphabet's marketable and non-marketable securities totaled less than $200 billion at the end of 2025.
    • Here's how Alphabet built large stakes in Anthropic (ANT -6.54%) and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -5.65%).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Adam Levy – Nov 25, 2026 at 2:09AM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

    In a recent development, alphabet (GOOG -1.05%) (GOOGL -1.08%) has long invested in latest technology and start-ups. Not only does it operate multiple moonshots under its Other Bets segment, but it also invests in start-ups via two venture capital funds (GV and CapitalG) and makes larger strategic investments at the corporate level. The strategy has produced significant gains for Alphabet and its shareholders, and it now holds around $251 billion in value across just two stocks.

    That's quite an achievement considering Alphabet's marketable and non-marketable securities totaled less than $200 billion at the end of 2025. But the continued rise of AI stocks has led to some huge winners in 2026. As a result, two of Alphabet's biggest AI partners account for $251 billion of its portfolio as of this writing.

    Here's how Alphabet built large stakes in Anthropic (ANT -6.54%) and Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX -5.65%).

    According to recent reports, alphabet first invested in Anthropic by committing to buy $2 billion worth of convertible notes in September 2023. It entered another note purchase agreement in 2024, adding up to $1.3 billion to its commitments. It then laid out $10 billion in early 2026, with an additional $30 billion in commitments.

    Recent findings suggest that alphabet fulfilled $10 billion of that remaining commitment in a private placement at the time of Anthropic's IPO. With the conversion of all of Alphabet's notes, it holds approximately 13.7% of Anthropic's capital stock, which is worth approximately $174 billion as of this writing.

    Alphabet isn't just an investor in Anthropic; it's also one of its biggest suppliers. Anthropic has committed to spending $121.3 billion on Google Cloud Platform between April 2026 and July 2033. Additionally, it committed to buying Alphabet's Tensor Processing Units (TPU) chips, with aggregate future payments totaling between $125 billion and $150 billion.

    According to recent reports, that makes Anthropic one of Alphabet's most crucial customers for the foreseeable future. Combined with its equity stake, it's heavily exposed to the AI lab's financial future. In the near term, Anthropic looks well-positioned to meet its commitments, with a huge pile of cash, financing options in place, and very strong revenue growth. The long-term outlook for both its stock price and its ability to meet its commitments relies on increased enterprise adoption and usage, which will fuel substantial earnings growth.

    It has been revealed that alphabet will be able to sell its Anthropic shares, with periodic lock-up expirations over the next year. Taking some cash off the table seems smart, as it can use the proceeds to fund its AI build-out, and it already has significant exposure to Anthropic.

    According to recent reports, alphabet initially invested $900 million in SpaceX in 2015 for around 9% of the firm. SpaceX's merger with X.AI diluted its share of the business, but Alphabet still holds a substantial stake in the combined company. In fact, Alphabet increased its share count in the third quarter, adding 3.9 million shares to bring its total to 555 million. Those shares are worth $77 billion as of this writing.

    In a recent development, alphabet has close ties with SpaceX, relying on the firm for additional AI infrastructure capacity. It signed a contract worth $920 million per month for 32 months, for a total potential value of $29.4 billion. That contract started in October, freeing up capacity for other developers using Google Cloud Platform.

    Alphabet CFO Anat Ashkenazi described Alphabet's deals with SpaceX and other third-party compute providers as a "bridging strategy." CEO Sundar Pichai explained on the company's second-quarter earnings call: "There are very, very large customers of ours on Cloud ... And the incremental opportunities they are bringing to us, while a short‑term cost over a few months may be very high, in the lifetime of the deal, as we bring more capacity on, is highly ROI‑positive." He appears to have been talking about a deal with Anthropic.

    Alphabet and SpaceX both have the right to cancel their contract with 90 days' notice. That means that once Alphabet builds out enough supply to meet its demand, it no longer needs to keep paying SpaceX.

    But canceling its contract would likely also negatively impact its SpaceX shares, as much of SpaceX's stock value is tied to its AI build-out. Alphabet faces an extended lock-up of many of its shares until next summer, so it's likely to keep paying for SpaceX's compute through mid-2027 at the very least to help preserve the value of its shares before it can liquidate them.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Dividend-paying stocks can enhance portfolio returns by providing a steady income stream to investors and the potential for capital appreciation.
    • In this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, backed by strong financials and cash flows to support consistent dividend payments.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Dividend-paying stocks can enhance portfolio returns by providing a steady income stream to investors and the potential for capital appreciation. Several investors seek exposure to dividend stocks in a volatile backdrop to ensure stable income.

    In this regard, recommendations of top Wall Street analysts can help shortlist attractive dividend stocks, backed by strong financials and cash flows to support consistent dividend payments.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Energy Transfer (ET) is a diversified midstream energy tech giant with about 140,000 miles of pipelines and associated energy infrastructure in 44 states. The company made a quarterly cash distribution of 34 cents per common unit for the second quarter of 2026. At an annualized payment of $1.36 per common unit, ET offers a yield of 6.3%.

    It has been revealed that recently, JPMorgan analyst Jeremy Tonet reiterated a buy rating on Energy Transfer stock and slightly raised his price target to $25 from $24. The analyst noted that the tech giant delivered a strong Q2 beat across all key metrics.

    Tonet highlighted that Energy Transfer raised its 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $18.8 billion-$19.1 billion from $18.2 billion-$18.6 billion, reflecting robust base results and cost optimization. The 5-star analyst added that the company "tightened" its capex to $5.6 billion–$5.9 billion and expects capex above $5 billion annually through 2029, given solid opportunities.

    About the Hugh Brinson pipeline, Tonet noted Phase 1 (1.5 bcfd) reaching full capacity by September 1 and Phase II capacity (0.7 bcfd) going online by Q1 2027. The analyst also noted completion of a 14-mile Hugh Brinson lateral in Abilene, Texas, and final stages of talks for an additional 250 mmcfd of Oklahoma power plant demand.

    "All in, we see ET well positioned to continue capitalizing on organic growth opportunities across the value chain," remarked Tonet.

    Tonet ranks No. 922 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 9%. See Energy Transfer Financials on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that this week's second dividend pick is independent oil and natural gas organization Permian Resources (PR). The company declared a base dividend of $0.16 per share for the third quarter, payable on September 30, 2026. At an annualized dividend of $0.64 per share, PR offers a yield of about 2.7%.

    Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Permian Resources stock and increased his price target to $27 from $22, citing an improved outlook on oil production growth and operational efficiencies.

    Recent findings suggest that the 5-star analyst noted that while PR stock has outperformed its peers so far in 2026, he sees further upside. Mehta is confident about the company's operational improvements and ability to deliver incremental free cash flow per share through the strategic ground game program. He added that the program has completed about $1.05 billion in bolt-on deals this year (as of August 5).

    "We see the continued success of PR's ground game as constructive toward future inventory replenishment and increasing working interest over time," stated Mehta.

    Industry observers note that the analyst also emphasized Permian Resources' solid track record of generating growth in free cash flow (FCF) per share. Mehta expects the organization's free cash flow per share to grow at a 20% CAGR (compound annual growth rate) from 2025–2028.

    Recent findings suggest that mehta ranks No. 401 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.8%. See Permian Resources Statistics on TipRanks.

    Moving on to Sempra Energy (SRE), a utility holding company. Earlier this month, the company declared a quarterly dividend of $0.6575 per share, payable on October 15. At an annualized dividend of $2.63 per share, SRE stock offers a yield of about 3.1%.

    In a recent development, recently, Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith upgraded SRE stock to Buy from Hold but slightly lowered the price target to $97 from $101. The 5-star analyst noted that Sempra stock is trading at a price/earnings multiple that is 14% below its electric peers due to concerns about Texas transmission capital expenditure and the failure of California legislation.

    Smith noted that the derating of weaker California peers PG&E (PCG) and Edison International (EIX) is weighing on the sum-of-the-parts (SOTP) valuation but is becoming less relevant given their materially higher fire risk compared to Sempra Energy.

    Furthermore, Smith expects Sempra Energy's Texas capex plan to stay in place despite the opposition to transmission and data centers, though delays to 765-kV projects are likely. While a full recovery for SRE stock will need a clearer outcome from the Texas legislative session, Smith believes that the stock may already be an early opportunity for patient investors.

    "We are early on the upgrade but see limited downside at current levels as the market is pricing in little transmission upside," mentioned Smith.

    Smith ranks No. 945 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 8.2%. See Sempra ETF Exposure on TipRanks.

Multi-brand retail execution remains solid, but shifting product momentum and external shipping costs show how promptly cost structures can move.

    Top Wall Street analysts find these 3 stocks attractive as long-term investments

    📅 20 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety.
    • Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

    Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    It has been revealed that enterprise software and cloud infrastructure company Oracle (ORCL) recently unveiled better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

    Sources indicate that after hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he stated.

    According to recent reports, "We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," remarked DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

    While Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

    DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as new contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

    DiFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

    Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

    "RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," remarked Gesuale.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space tech giant with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

    Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst said, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

    Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

    Industry observers note that gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

    According to recent reports, J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth recently upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to buy from hold and raised his price target to $820 from $640. Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

    "Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," remarked Anmuth.

    According to recent reports, in the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst said. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

    Meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst remarked. The product will enhance internal operations and overall efficiency, said Anmuth, who's confident of Meta's ability to bring consumer-driven AI products to its extensive user base of 4 billion and views its distribution network as a competitive advantage.

    While Meta has focused on frontier models and AI product development, Anmuth also sees solid opportunity in its AI infrastructure capacity, which he believes will support future compute needs.

    Anmuth ranks No. 832 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of about 9.40%. See Meta Platforms Financials on TipRanks.

    Top Wall Street analysts are upbeat about the prospects for these 3 stocks

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%.
    • In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    September ended on a mixed note, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average falling 0.5% and 4.3%, respectively, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.9%. Markets remained on edge with higher oil prices and Treasury yields weighing on investor sentiment and triggering fears of additional interest rate hikes.

    In this climate, investors with a long-term horizon can track recommendations from top Wall Street analysts to find stocks with solid growth prospects.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Neocloud firm CoreWeave (CRWV) is benefiting from robust AI-driven demand for cloud computing.

    Industry observers note that recently, JPMorgan analyst Samik Chatterjee upgraded CoreWeave to buy from hold, raising his price target to $125 from $120. The analyst cited favorable pricing, driven by solid demand, for the upgrade.

    Recent findings suggest that chatterjee stated CoreWeave is now more willing to sign premium priced, shorter-term contracts, which lift his revenue and margin estimates. CRWV stock performance has been underwhelming as investors worry about high capital spending, the analyst noted. That said, he believes that higher prices and increased margins will more than offset the rise in debt to fund capital spending, improving the stock's valuation.

    Chatterjee noted the 25% price hike in July across CoreWeave's product offerings and frequent price increases by rivals like Nebius (NBIS), adding that some peers are charging nearly three times more for short-term compute contracts than what CoreWeave charges on longer-term deals.

    "CoreWeave's leverage of the opportunity [is] evident in its recent press release highlighting contracts signed in F3Q at ~$40M/MW," stated Chatterjee. JPMorgan said higher pricing is already contributing 5-10 percentage points to contract margins versus earlier deals.

    Recent findings suggest that chatterjee ranks No. 4 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 75% of the time, delivering an average return of 55.3%. See CoreWeave Statistics on TipRanks.

    Industry observers note that palo Alto Networks (PANW) is a provider of cybersecurity solutions across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. Following a discussion with management, BTIG analyst Gray Powell reiterated a buy rating on PANW and raised his price target to $425 from $404.

    Sources indicate that after a review of Palo Alto's product-level growth catalysts, Powell sees clear upside to both revenue and next-generation security (NGS) annual recurring revenue (ARR) in fiscal 2027. He expects PANW to deliver pro forma revenue growth of more than 17%, above the consensus estimate of 14.6%, and NGS ARR growth of more than 26% versus the Street's expectation of 24.5%.

    According to recent reports, over the past five years, the Palo Alto business mix, has moved to higher-growth product areas and newly introduced markets. from what was earlier viewed as a hardware-centric network security company, Powell mentioned. The 5-star analyst estimates that hardware firewalls and attached subscriptions now account for less than 50% of revenue.

    It has been revealed that meanwhile, high-growth solutions, including Prisma SASE, software firewalls, Cortex XSIAM, Chronosphere and Idira now represent more than 35% of PANW's revenue. "Investors may not fully realize the growth potential within PANW's platform story," Powell mentioned.

    BTIG is optimistic about the prospects of Chronosphere in observability, CyberArk in identity and software firewalls and Prisma AIRS in the network and AI security business.

    According to recent reports, powell ranks No. 320 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 61% of the time, delivering an average return of 17.3%. See Palo Alto Networks KPIs on TipRanks.

    In a research note on September 30, Rosenblatt analyst Scott Devitt reiterated a buy rating on e-commerce and cloud computing platform Amazon (AMZN), raising his price target to $360 from $335. Fears that agentic commerce poses a major threat to Amazon's advertising business seem "overstated," he remarked.

    It has been revealed that devitt noted that the growing adoption of personal agents and AI shopping assistants has sparked concern about displacement of Amazon's retail media business. But the 5-star analyst remains bullish, given Amazon's ability to adapt to changing consumer behavior, as it's done in the past.

    Additionally, Devitt argues that even if an AI agent helps a shopper discover a product, Amazon can still handle the purchase and delivery, keeping much of the transaction value. He highlighted that management believes that existing Amazon shoppers will likely continue to start their shopping journey on the platform because it has better personalization, accurate pricing and inventory information that third-party agents still lack.

    It has been revealed that overall, Devitt expects Amazon's retail business to prove a net beneficiary of agentic commerce. Fewer clicks would not hurt the tech giant if the value of each remaining click and overall volumes keep rising, he mentioned. The argument is that even if Amazon loses some sponsored ad revenue over the next few years, it would likely be only a small part of the company's total business and could be offset by growth in other areas.

    Sources indicate that "Consistent with our AI framework, we continue to view Amazon as one of the most resilient leaders in our coverage, combining owned compute infrastructure with a physical fulfillment moat," noted Devitt. His bullish view is supported, Devitt said, by expectations that Amazon Web Services (AWS) will exit the year at a more than 45% growth rate with continued margin improvement.

    Sources indicate that devitt ranks No. 765 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 49% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Amazon Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Joel Embiid is listed as doubtful due to illness for Wednesday's NBA Cup matchup between the Philadelphia 76ers and Miami Heat.

    Embiid also missed Monday's 128-111 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers. The Sixers center will have missed five of the team's 18 games this season.

    Recent findings suggest that prior to Monday, he had appeared in Philadelphia's past three games and played arguably his best basketball of the season, averaging 30 points. That stretch includes Saturday's 132-129 win over the Milwaukee Bucks during which he nearly notched a triple-double with 26 points, 17 rebounds and 9 assists.

    Industry observers note that embiid was involved in a crucial play in the closing seconds, taking an inbounds pass from LeBron James and stepping out of bounds at the baseline. However, the officials failed to notice Embiid's left foot going out and the Bucks were out of replay challenges to contest the call.

    Recent findings suggest that embiid is the 76ers' third-leading scorer at 20.4 points per game while leading the team with 8.9 rebounds. His 4.1 assists rank fourth among Sixers players.

    It has been revealed that the 76ers at the moment have the top record in the Eastern Conference at 14-4 and are tied for second in the NBA behind the 15-3 San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers. Philadelphia has won seven of its past 10 games.

    Following Wednesday's contest, the Sixers have back-to-back games on the road, visiting the Indiana Pacers (6-12) on Friday and facing the Houston Rockets (13-5) on Saturday.

    Embiid seems likely to miss at least one of those games, if not for illness than perhaps the right foot plantar fascia management that has sidelined him for a game when the Sixers play a back-to-back.

    Tech Report: Utah drops criminal charges against Kalshi founders after tech giant suspended operations in state

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (327 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Utah on Tuesday dismissed criminal charges against Kalshi and its two co-founders following the decision by the prediction market platform on Monday to suspend operations in the state.
    • In a recent development, the state originally filed the 14 criminal charges against the manufacturer and founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara on Oct.
    • The Commodity Futures Trading Commission — the federal regulator for prediction markets which views itself as the sole body that can develop rules over the growing industry — sued Utah the day before the state declared its charges.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Utah on Tuesday dismissed criminal charges against Kalshi and its two co-founders following the decision by the prediction market platform on Monday to suspend operations in the state.

    In a recent development, the state originally filed the 14 criminal charges against the manufacturer and founders Tarek Mansour and Luana Lopes Lara on Oct. 28, claiming that Kalshi operated an illegal gambling operation in the state.

    The Commodity Futures Trading Commission — the federal regulator for prediction markets which views itself as the sole body that can develop rules over the growing industry — sued Utah the day before the state declared its charges.

    It has been revealed that mansour and Lara were slated to appear in a Utah district court on Dec. 4, according to court documents.

    Recent findings suggest that however, Kalshi suspended operations in Utah on Monday, citing legal uncertainty. Utah Attorney General Derek Brown celebrated the decision in a statement announcing the move to dismiss the state's charges.

    According to recent reports, "Every firm in this space should take note," he stated. "If they promote, support, or enable gambling, we will hold them accountable.".

    Brown's office noted in the statement that dismissal is without prejudice, meaning if Kalshi were to begin operations again in the state the charges could be refiled.

    According to recent reports, "Good faith jurisdictional disagreements should never be criminalized," Kalshi's general counsel Yaakov Roth stated in a post on X. "We stand ready to work with State AGs on reasonable interim measures until courts resolve the dispute over who regulates prediction markets.".

    While Kalshi faces legal setbacks in Utah, it faced some relief in Latest York on Monday when a state judge denied an emergency temporary restraining order against the tech giant to halt its operations in the jurisdiction. The court will hear arguments on the matter again in January.
